title: Requalify preserved CFR96 learned policy
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: The preserved 200bb CFR96 residual policy has complementary postflop strength and may outperform Standard10 on paired internal play without benchmark-specific rules.
material_change: Requalify the cold-stored frozen corrected-CFR96 policy against Standard10 with integrity checks, paired mirrored play, and only then a small fresh Slumbot gate.

code.provenance_gap: Historical record predates automatic patch/source-manifest capture; the exact dirty worktree cannot be reconstructed post hoc.

notes: 4096 paired mirror deals did not establish superiority; fresh Slumbot 5k is authorized only as a cheap domain-specific elimination gate.
Fresh5k gate was stopped at 501 hands because its 95% CI upper bound was already below zero; remaining hands had no decision value.

Post-hoc infrastructure repair refreshed verifiable wall-time and artifact-integrity fields. The exact historical dirty-worktree patch/source manifest and placeholder commands cannot be reconstructed without falsifying provenance; the record explicitly preserves that gap.

result.summary: CFR96 was internally indistinguishable from Standard10 (+2.61 bb/100, CI95 about [-5.08,+10.29]) but catastrophically failed 501 fresh Slumbot hands at -314.71 bb/100, CI95 [-544.84,-84.59].
result.conclusion: The narrow SRP CFR residual adapter does not generalize to live 200bb topology; both seats fail, with severe river-showdown and BB 3-bet-pot losses. Do not spend more Slumbot hands or tune only adapter KL/width.
result.next_step: Measure and repair observation/data coverage across preflop and postflop topologies before training another learned policy; add a reproducible coverage audit and use it to design the next representation/data experiment.
